issues.description: Method name mismatch for Pneumatic.openValve(): The UML in the problem statement (interface Pneumatic) declares an abstract method openValve(). In the solution, the Pneumatic interface declares a method named releaseValve() (src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java line 7), while the concrete classes LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement a method named openValve() (src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedDropdownTower.java line 15 and src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedRollerCoaster.java line 15). This naming inconsistency means the implementing classes do not actually implement the interface method as declared, which will cause compilation errors and will confuse students about the required method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Preferably rename releaseValve() in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java to openValve() so the interface matches the UML and the concrete classes. Alternatively, rename the openValve() methods in the implementing classes to releaseValve() and update the UML/problem statement accordingly. After renaming, ensure all declarations, implementations, and the UML/problem statement consistently use the same method name and keep the parameter/return signature unchanged.
